text:
tia: FYI onboarding run tripped a nasty embed/rerank bug tied to batching helper retries + serializer parity. Scores were being applied to the wrong ids and some vectors lost padding.

harry: Yikes. Can you paste the tiny repro and logs?

tia: Repro summary: sampleapp uses the official batch helper. Flow: split into chunks -> send -> server returns 502 for first chunk -> SDK auto-retries. During reassembly the helper concatenates buffers and sometimes reorders items. We log the original request as: 
```
{"items":[{"id":"doc-A","vec":[0.1,0.2,0.3]},{"id":"doc-B","vec":[0.5,0.6]},{"id":"doc-C","vec":[0.9,0.8,0.7]}]}
```
After retry reassembly observed payloads like doc-B,doc-A,doc-C and B's vector lost padding. The server returns scores in positional order so consumers mapping by index get wrong assignments.

ana: Does this happen only in Node?

tia: Node shows it consistently due to Buffer/Float32Array concat path. Python shows flakier behavior with async concurrency >4.

harry: Two issues: (A) concat reassembly must be stable, and (B) response shapes diverge across helper code-paths (flat vs nested). We must never rely on index-only mapping.

ana: Short-term mitigation for customers: always include an explicit stable id per item and post-process mapping by id. Also add a dim-validation step before doing cosine similarity. Example snippet for mapping: 
```
// pseudo
const scoreMap = {};
const scores = resp.scores || (resp.results && resp.results.scores) || [];
ids.forEach((id,i)=> scoreMap[id] = scores[i] ?? null);
```
But ideally server should echo per-item ids to remove index dependence.

ci-bot: flakiness-detector: reproduced locally with randomized reorder seed=7.

tia: Filed DE-10234: helper reassembly determinism + serializer parity + per-item response ids. Assigned eng-runtime + eng-ml.

devex-bot: DE-10234 created and linked to #eng-runtime.

harry: Quick patch idea for helpers: (1) attach a monotonic "_seq" to each item, (2) never mutate original arrays in-place, build a new reassembly array copying references, (3) include item id in response mapping from server.

ana: Also add a server-side guard: if incoming batch metadata indicates per-item id list, server should include ids in the response, even on partial success. That fixes clients that map by id.

tia: I repro'd an auth-refresh interplay too: when token refresh happens mid-batch the helper sometimes strips batch headers causing the server to treat chunks separately and return different JSON shapes.

harry: That's likely why Node and Python had different serializer output. We'll add serializer parity tests simulating token expiry + 502 + retry.

ci-bot: test-plan-suggestion: add integration test that simulates token expiry mid-batch, forces 502 on first attempt, then succeeds; randomize reassembly and assert final request order equals original order using _seq.

ana: Short-term patch for sampleapp: (1) validate dims, reject mixed lengths or pad explicitly, (2) map responses by id, (3) assert response shape and normalize both flat and nested shapes. I'll open a PR.

harry: Let's plan a minor helper release with the deterministic reassembly and _seq field. Target this week.

tia: I'll update onboarding docs: add checklist item "always attach stable ids and validate dims when using embed/rerank batching with retries" and include the mapping snippet.

devex-bot: Note: add lint rule proposal to DE-10234 to warn when mixed vector lengths are batched without explicit padding.

harry: Thanks team. Follow DE-10234 for the runtime/SDK fixes. Resolved for the sampleapp case. :thumbsup:
